title: Move a frozen sample between cold boxes within 20 seconds
instruction: Move the magenta sample vial from the left cold box into the right cold box. The vial must spend no more than 20 seconds in total outside the cold boxes.
context: Frozen biological samples start to thaw within seconds at room temperature, so labs move them between cold boxes quickly. Neither arm reaches both boxes, so the arms must relay the vial through the middle without delay.
setup: Two arm bases stand 61 cm apart at the near edge of a table; positions are measured forward from the line through the bases and sideways from the midline between them. Two blue cold boxes (open-top, 14 x 14 cm inside, walls 1 cm thick and 5 cm tall, foam board, with a pale blue floor plate 4 mm thick; fixed) are centred 27 cm out, one 30 cm left and one 30 cm right of the midline. A magenta sample vial (a cylinder 4 cm wide and 6 cm tall, plastic, 30 g) stands in the middle of the left box. A grey plastic transfer pad (10 x 10 cm, 4 mm thick, fixed) is centred 25 cm out on the midline. The arms start in their folded ready pose. Each arm reaches only its own box and the pad.
scoring: The vial is outside whenever it is not down in a box: its centre over a box's inside and its bottom below the box's 5 cm rim. Time outside is the total over the trial, from the video at 20 frames per second. For a vial resting in the right box at the end: 1.0 if it spent at most 20 s outside, 0.5 at most 30 s, 0.25 at most 45 s. Otherwise 0, including a vial not in the right box at the end, more than 45 s outside, or more than 5 cm below the table top (off the table).
reset_notes: Stand the vial back in the middle of the left box.
fidelity: Approximate: no temperature is simulated; the cold boxes are open-top and the time limit stands in for thawing. The vial is a rigid cylinder with the simulator's default contact friction; it may come to rest on its side in the box, which still counts as inside.
